svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS DA — Appendix A · AppA_AlgebraicNT, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 747 declarations of the 121 items on CA, each with its kind, file, line and state; 65 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

g.text: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 747 declarations of the 121 items on CA, each with its kind, file, line and state; 65 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of CA's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card, and under it, in italics, the first sentence of its first declaration's docstring, quoted. Then the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: The restricted product consists of the tuples eventually in the distinguished subgroups.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The printed Cartesian product does not provide the two subsets used in the definition. We use a finite subset of exceptional indices and its complement.

g.text: The infinite factor is the real scalar extension of the field, the finite factor is the restricted product of the nonarchimedean completions, and their product carries the adelic topology.

g.text: the sign is opposite to the printed exp(2πit). With the printed sign at the real place (Example A.3.1.5) and at the p-adic places, the product character of Example A.3.1.8 takes the value exp(4πi/3) on the rational number 1/3. It must be trivial on the rationals for Theorem 2.2.3.2 and Theorem 3.2.2.1, as in Tate's thesis, where the two kinds of place carry opposite signs. The

g.text: This records the symmetry clause at positive indices using normSectionNeighborhood. The printed formula divides by zero at index zero. The finite factor is the one at S in (A.5.2.21), which this lemma cites. Its introductory sentence on p. 577 names the full finite unit group.
